rules.newest: Only the newest generation of each line is used (Sonnet 5.5, not Sonnet 5); the older ones are superseded.
rules.offered: Only a model the CLI of a chosen harness lists is in, whatever Artificial Analysis lists; a model only the lane table names is not offered.
rules.profiled: Every model has a profile written from its maker's pages, with its sources and the date checked; without one the build exits 1.

profile.purpose: "For high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as classification, extraction, and routing." Its model page adds: "built for high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as classification, routing, extraction, and subagent tasks." Comparative latency: fastest.

price.note: per million tokens for a prompt up to 100,000 tokens; a prompt over 100,000 tokens pays $0.50 in and $2.50 out, five times as much, and the length counts every input token, cache reads and writes included; cache reads at $0.01 ($0.05 over 100,000), batch at 50% off

profile.availability: Claude API id claude-haiku-5-5; released 2026-10-07, not retired before 2027-10-07. Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Each harness takes the efforts its entry lists.
caveats: Adaptive thinking is on by default and effort is its main control; thinking can be disabled only at high effort or below, and a request that disables it at xhigh or max returns a 400 error.
At low effort in long agent prompts the model is more likely to skip a search, stop early, or skip a check (Anthropic's effort page): start at medium.
Its tokenizer counts the same text as about 30% more tokens than Claude Haiku 4.5.
It is the only current Claude model priced by prompt length; the others include the full 1M window at one price.

profile.purpose: "The best combination of speed and intelligence." Comparative latency: fast.

price.note: per million tokens; cache reads at 5% of the input price, batch at 50% off

profile.availability: Claude API id claude-sonnet-5-5; not retired before 2027-09-28. Each harness takes the efforts its entry lists.
caveats: Adaptive thinking: the model decides how much to think, steered by effort.

profile.purpose: "For long-running agentic coding and knowledge work." Anthropic's advice: start here for most workloads, and move to Fable 5.1 when evals on Opus 5.5 at higher effort still fall short. Comparative latency: moderate.

price.note: per million tokens; cache reads at 5% of the input price, batch at 50% off

profile.availability: Claude API id claude-opus-5-5; not retired before 2027-09-22. Each harness takes the efforts its entry lists.
caveats: Thinking is always on (adaptive).

profile.purpose: A flagship reasoning model, with a unified 1M context window and long decodes up to 1M tokens.

price.note: per million tokens through 2026-11-30 (cached input 0.1), and double from 2026-12-01 (cached input 0.2), by Google's pricing page, with one rate for every prompt size; OpenRouter and Artificial Analysis list 2 and 10 on 2026-10-15

profile.availability: Stable in the Gemini API (id gemini-4-argon). Rolled out on 2026-10-13 to Google AI Pro and Ultra in the Gemini app. `agy models` 1.3.6 lists it as gemini-4-argon-low, -medium and -high on the owner's machine from 2026-10-15, and the Judge, Examiner and Writer seats each ran a round on it that day.
caveats: agy takes it at low, medium and high; it has no xhigh, so the pair rule asks it only for the efforts it takes.
Not measured against the native Judge yet (R16 of spec 001): the seeded-defects harness found 6 of 6 defects in one round per fixture, which shows that it works, not that it matches Opus.
Inputs, outputs and cutoff are not on the pages read.

excluded.reason: The owner keeps Fable out until Fable 5.5 (decision A43).

profile.purpose: "For demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work." Anthropic's advice: for most workloads start with Opus 5.5, and use Fable 5.1 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, or when evals on Opus 5.5 at higher effort still fall short. Comparative latency: slower.

price.note: per million tokens; cache reads at 2.5% of the input price ($0.25), batch at 50% off

profile.availability: Claude API id claude-fable-5-1; released 2026-09-01, not retired before 2027-09-01. Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Each harness takes the efforts its entry lists.
caveats: Thinking is always on (adaptive), and it is the only thinking mode.
Forced tool use returns an error, and only Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 can read its thinking blocks, which editing earlier turns invalidates.
Claude Mythos 5.1 has the same capabilities and the same price, and is offered only to organizations Anthropic's verification programs have verified.

withoutFigures.note: offered, with no Artificial Analysis entry, so no figures; not a lane: the lane table does not list it

profile.purpose: The same Grok 4.7 served on faster infrastructure: faster and dearer, not a different or smaller model.

price.note: 2x the Grok 4.7 token rates (1.5x for long-context requests), per the docs; billed through the plan in Cursor and Grok Build, not through the API

profile.availability: Only in Cursor and Grok Build, billed through the plan there; not in Grok Build's free tier; not on the public xAI API.
caveats: Not a cheap lane: it is billed through the plan at twice the token price of Grok 4.7, and the lane table does not list it.
xAI's page does not give the model id and does not mention `build-fast`: that this id is the Fast variant rests on the owner's word and on `grok models` listing it.
The docs do not state the speed multiple; third-party sites say about 2x output speed.
Artificial Analysis has no entry for it, so it has no scores here; its quality is Grok 4.7's.
